name: Cade Johnson
caption: NTICW's founding president, hospitalized in critical condition in December 2002 and eased out of ownership by a buyout two months later.
notes: The fed's own December 2002 rumours page billed him President and reported him hospitalized in critical condition under circumstances the page leaves a mystery, adding that Vice-President Chris Harmon was awaiting trial for attempted vehicular manslaughter against him. The February 2003 news page reports a large sum of money "offered and laid down on the table in recent weeks" to Johnson before an unnamed buyer purchased the federation and installed Kyle Crossett as CEO; Johnson does not appear again after this.

tenures.role: authority-figure — President, later reported to have sold the federation

name: Chris Harmon
caption: NTICW's vice-president, billed awaiting trial for attempted vehicular manslaughter against the president he was accused of putting in the hospital.

identity.note: A bare-name collision, surfaced by the standing mint guard, against an authority-figure minted for NGW's own AW/NTW-branded storyline, same 2002 era. No held document on either side names the other fed, or claims a shared performer/character. Filed distinct pending evidence, per the collision doctrine — when in doubt we do not merge.

tenures.role: authority-figure — Vice-President; billed awaiting trial for attempted vehicular manslaughter against President Cade Johnson, expected to be removed from his position on Johnson's return to work

name: Peter Degennaro
caption: Wrestled a tag match on NTICW's debut Mayhem while running its operations, then vanished without explanation.

tenures.role: authority-figure and wrestler — billed both "CEO of Operations" and, one paragraph later on the same page, "Vice President of Operations"; the fed's own rumours page reports he wrestled a tag match on the debut Mayhem and then disappeared, not heard from since

name: Kyle Crossett
caption: Installed as NTICW's CEO by an unnamed buyer in February 2003, and fronted the fed's own relaunch signings.
notes: Billed a former staffer of "the legendary indy fed NrCw" (unaccessioned — see the museum's own frontier), where the news page says he crossed paths with new signee Kris Korbyn: "These two men have had confrontations previously in their careers, but have also been known to be on a very trusting level." Quoted at length on the fed's own news page denying a reporter's suggestion that NTICW was cursed: "NTICW is anything but cursed... Cursed?! You have to be [censored] kidding me!"

identity.note: A decorated-name collision against an unrelated existing "Kyle Cross" row, surfaced by the mint guard. No held document on either side connects the two. Filed distinct under the collision doctrine, not merged.

tenures.role: authority-figure — CEO, installed by an unnamed new owner after Cade Johnson's ouster; does not hold ownership himself

notes: Resurrection's own promotion, roster and dates are not named anywhere in the corpus — recorded as a former affiliation only, not minted as a unit. Rumored by the fed's own news page to be very close to CEO Crossett, for reasons the page itself says are left unknown.
